import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
df['Total_Spending'] = df[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Create a bar plot of average total spending by education level
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=df, x='Education', y='Total_Spending', ci=None, palette='viridis')

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Average Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Average Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
df['Total_Spending'] = df[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Create a bar plot of average total spending by education level
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=df, x='Education', y='Total_Spending', ci=None, palette='viridis')

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Average Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Average Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
